claim: In 615 adults followed prospectively after epilepsy surgery (497 anterior temporal resections; median follow-up 8 years), Kaplan-Meier estimates of remaining seizure free (apart from simple partial seizures) were 52% at 5 years and 47% at 10 years; extratemporal resections had higher recurrence than anterior temporal resections (HR 2.0).

bibliographic_record.authors: de Tisi J, Bell GS, Peacock JL, McEvoy AW, Harkness WF, Sander JW, Duncan JS
bibliographic_record.title: The long-term outcome of adult epilepsy surgery, patterns of seizure remission, and relapse: a cohort study

supporting_passage: We used survival methods to estimate that 52% (95% CI 48-56) of patients remained seizure free (apart from simple partial seizures [SPS]) at 5 years after surgery, and 47% (42-51) at 10 years.
passage_location: Abstract, Findings section. Abstract only (full text not read). Europe PMC REST API (resultType=core, abstractText) for PMID 22000136; https://europepmc.org/abstract/MED/22000136; accessed 2026-11-01

population_and_design.design: single-centre prospective cohort with annual follow-up (UK, NHNN/UCL)

endpoint.reported_endpoint: time to first seizure (excluding simple partial seizures), Kaplan-Meier; approximates ILAE 1-2 / Engel I continuous seizure freedom
endpoint.protocol_mapping_v1: seizure free apart from SPS -> favourable (equivalent to ILAE 2 / Engel I criterion; to_verify)

reported_observation: 52% at 5 y and 47% at 10 y continuously seizure free (apart from SPS); 104/365 (28%) seizure-free patients off drugs at last follow-up.
author_inference: Surgery is appealing for selected people with refractory focal epilepsy; data give realistic expectations.
contradictions: Lower than the 66% median long-term seizure freedom after temporal resection pooled by Tellez-Zenteno 2005; difference plausibly due to stricter survival (time-to-first-seizure) definition vs cross-sectional definitions.
